digest.top_line: KEYNOTE-975: pembro + dCRT EFS 15.2 vs 14.7 mo, HR 0.97 (0.77-1.23) in CPS ≥10 locally advanced unresectable esophageal/GEJ cancer; trial stopped, no IO add-on to dCRT.
digest.tldr: Two RT readouts, no OS gain. KEYNOTE-975 adds no EFS with pembro to dCRT in CPS ≥10, plus more grade 5 AEs; SARON consolidation RT in synchronous OM AGA-negative NSCLC cut 12-mo local failure 13.0% vs 39.5% and improved PFS (HR 0.64), OS HR 0.99. MATISSE 2 interim: 71% skip surgery ± adjuvant RT after NIVO/IPI in CSCC.

sites.intro: Ultra-short neoadjuvant IO in CSCC raises surgery and adjuvant RT omission, on 8-mo f/u only.

studies.name: MATISSE 2
studies.tldr: 71% (22/31) clinical response at week 5 with SOC withheld, 48% CCR, after ultra-short neoadjuvant NIVO/IPI in CSCC; median f/u 8 mo.
details: 🔍 CSCC with indication for extensive or disfiguring curative surgery; 41 planned, 31 included so far
💊 NIVO weeks 0 & 2 + IPI week 0 only; no maintenance IO
🔍 Response evaluated week 5; non-responders proceed to SOC week 6
🔍 Clinical responders skip SOC (surgery ± adjuvant RT) → strict wait-and-monitoring
📊 1 of 9 SOC pts had complete pathological response in surgical specimen
📊 Grade 3-4 irAEs 19%; no surgical delay from immune toxicity
🔗 Builds on MATISSE (NCT04620200): 80% partial/major pathological response after 2 courses NIVO/IPI, 9 CCRs
⚠️ Median f/u 8 mo; durability of CCR without surgery or RT unknown
⚠️ CCR is a clinical, not pathological, endpoint; no biopsy confirmation reported
⚠️ Interim report, 31 of 41 planned pts; no comparator arm

verdict.rationale: Interim report of a non-comparative cohort, 31/41 accrued, 8 mo median f/u; clinical response without pathological confirmation for most pts.
verdict.audience: CSCC needing extensive/disfiguring curative surgery ± adjuvant RT

studies.significance: The SOC being withheld here is surgery with or without adjuvant RT, so 22/31 (71%) responders skipped both, with 7/31 (23%) still only partial responders under surveillance. Partial responders carry the local-failure risk that would land on salvage surgery or RT, and 8 mo median f/u cannot yet show how many convert or progress.
studies.monday_clinic: In CSCC where curative surgery would be extensive or disfiguring, this supports considering trial referral for neoadjuvant NIVO/IPI with response-adapted omission of surgery and adjuvant RT; it does not extend to off-trial omission of SOC or to resectable CSCC without that morbidity.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Response-adapted organ-preservation trial, **41 pts planned, 31 included**, median follow-up **8 mo**. Response evaluated at week 5; non-responders go to SOC at week 6, clinical responders enter **strict wait-and-monitoring**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: CSCC with an indication for **extensive or disfiguring curative surgery**, with or without adjuvant RT, as SOC.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **Nivolumab weeks 0 and 2, ipilimumab week 0 only.** No maintenance immunotherapy.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: RT is not delivered by protocol to responders; adjuvant RT is part of the SOC that is **withheld** after clinical response. RT dose, volumes, and use in the 9 SOC pts are not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **22/31 (71%)** clinical response and no SOC; **15/31 (48%) CCR**, 7/31 (23%) PCR. 9/31 (29%) received SOC, 1 with complete pathological response.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Grade 3-4 immune-related toxicity **19%**. No surgical delay attributed to immune toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: MATISSE (NCT04620200) established the pathological response signal with 2 courses of NIVO/IPI followed by surgery and found 9 CCRs without SOC. MATISSE 2 tests whether that clinical response can replace surgery and adjuvant RT outright.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents CSCC pts facing extensive or disfiguring curative surgery ± adjuvant RT. Does not represent CSCC managed with limited excision, or pts ineligible for combined checkpoint blockade.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: CCR is judged clinically rather than by pathology, so the false-negative rate of week 5 assessment is unknown. The 7 PCR pts are being observed with residual disease, and their outcome will decide whether watchful waiting is safe.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The result shows an organ-preservation strategy is feasible after only 3 doses of IO. It does not yet show that skipping surgery and RT is oncologically equivalent; that needs local recurrence and salvage data with longer follow-up.

studies.interpretation:
The MATISSE program moves the question in CSCC from whether checkpoint blockade works before surgery to whether it can replace surgery and adjuvant RT. The first MATISSE trial answered the earlier question: 80% partial or major pathological response after two courses of NIVO/IPI, and 9 pts reaching clinical complete remission without SOC. MATISSE 2 acts on that observation by making it the protocol. Week 5 clinical response triggers omission of SOC, and in this interim cohort 22/31 (71%) pts avoided surgery and any adjuvant RT that would have followed.

The number a reader should weigh most is not the 71% but the split beneath it. 15/31 (48%) reached CCR, while 7/31 (23%) are partial clinical responders being observed with residual disease. Watching a CCR is a familiar organ-preservation posture, comparable in logic to watch-and-wait after neoadjuvant therapy in rectal cancer. Observing a partial response without definitive local therapy is a bolder choice, and the abstract frames it as a bet on response deepening over time. Whether that bet pays off is the central unknown, because these are pts whose disease warranted extensive or disfiguring surgery in the first place. A local failure in that group may be harder to salvage than the original tumor.

The methodology should temper confidence in two directions. First, response is assessed clinically at week 5, and pathology is only available for the 9 pts who went to SOC. One of those 9 had a complete pathological response, which means clinical assessment classified at least one pathological complete responder as a non-responder. The reverse error, clinical CCR with viable residual tumor, cannot be measured in this design and is the error that matters for omission. Second, median follow-up is 8 months. Immunotherapy responses can be durable, but they can also relapse locally, and the time course of regrowth after only three doses with no maintenance is not characterized.

For radiation oncologists the trial is quietly an RT omission study. Adjuvant RT for high-risk CSCC is part of the SOC being withheld, and the source does not break out how many responders would have received it. If the strategy holds, RT shifts from adjuvant to salvage in this population, and the relevant data to watch for are local recurrence rates, time to salvage, and whether salvage RT or surgery succeeds after IO-induced regression.

The toxicity profile is acceptable for a curative-intent approach, at 19% grade 3-4 immune-related events and no surgical delays. What would make this result wrong is a pattern of late local recurrence among partial responders that converts organ preservation into delayed, more morbid salvage. Full accrual and mature local control data are the gate.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Adjuvant RT is part of the withheld SOC, so responders skip RT entirely and RT shifts toward salvage. Local recurrence and salvage outcomes in the 7/31 partial responders under surveillance will decide whether omitting adjuvant RT is safe.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Three doses total (NIVO weeks 0 and 2, IPI week 0) with no maintenance produced 48% CCR at 19% grade 3-4 irAEs. The open regimen question is durability off therapy and whether partial responders deepen without further IO.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: 71% of pts slated for extensive or disfiguring resection avoided surgery at week 5. The 7/31 partial responders under observation with residual disease carry the salvage risk, and 1 of 9 resected non-responders was a pathological complete responder, so week 5 clinical assessment misclassifies in at least one direction.

open_questions: Durability of CCR without surgery, RT, or maintenance IO
Do partial clinical responders deepen or recur locally?
Salvage success after local failure under wait-and-monitoring

studies.name: [212Pb]VMT-α-NET
studies.tldr: No DLTs, G4/5 AEs, or serious renal events across 67 pts; ORR 43.4% in a cohort 2 subset (n=23/46), SSTR2+ progressive NETs.
details: 🔍 Phase 1/2a dose escalation, alpha-emitting SSTR2-targeted radiopharmaceutical
🔍 Unresectable/metastatic NETs, radiologic progression after ≥1 prior systemic line, SSTR2+ on FDA-approved SSTR PET
💊 Up to 4 administrations at assigned dose level; DLT window 42 days

details.text: 📊 Safety, all 67 treated pts: none observed of

details: 📊 Cohort 2 ORR 43.4% (RECIST v1.1, investigator-assessed), previously reported subset n=23/46, f/u 60.1 wks
📊 Cohort 3: 2 PRs after 1 and 2 cycles; both Cohort 1 pts SD at 2 yrs
⚠️ Full 56-pt efficacy set results not given in abstract; ORR comes from the earlier subset only
⚠️ Investigator-assessed response, no central review stated; no PFS or DoR reported in source
🔗 Context: 177Lu-DOTATATE (NETTER-1) is the beta-emitter SSTR2 benchmark; no head-to-head data here

verdict.rationale: Single-arm phase 1/2a dose escalation; efficacy from a 23-pt subset, investigator-read, no PFS or durability data, no comparator vs beta-emitter RLT.
verdict.audience: SSTR2+ unresectable/metastatic NETs, progressed after ≥1 systemic line

studies.significance: The dosimetry-limiting organs read clean so far: no serious renal events and no clinically significant treatment-related myelosuppression across 67 pts through the 6 mCi level, with escalation continuing into Cohort 4. The response figure is the 43.4% from 23 cohort 2 pts; the 56-pt efficacy set is not reported in source.
studies.monday_clinic: In SSTR2+ progressive NETs after ≥1 systemic line, this supports trial referral for alpha-emitter RLT rather than any change in off-trial sequencing.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Phase 1/2a **dose-escalation** trial (NCT05636618); DLT monitoring for **42 days**, safety throughout. Efficacy by investigator RECIST v1.1.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Unresectable or metastatic NETs** with radiologic progression after **≥1 prior systemic treatment** and SSTR2 expression in ≥1 lesion on FDA-approved SSTR PET.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Up to **4 administrations** of [212Pb]VMT-α-NET at the assigned dose: **2.5 mCi** (n=2), **5 mCi** (n=46), **6 mCi** (n=19). Cohort 4 now enrolling.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Cohort 2 **ORR 43.4%** in the previously presented subset (n=23/46). Cohort 3: **2 PRs** after 1 and 2 cycles. Cohort 1: both pts **stable disease after 2 years**.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **No DLTs, no G4/5 AEs**, no treatment-related discontinuations, serious renal events, dysphagia, or clinically significant myelosuppression in 67 treated pts.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: 177Lu-DOTATATE (NETTER-1) defines SSTR2-targeted RLT; this is the alpha-emitter counterpart. No comparative data, and prior-RLT exposure is not reported, so relative activity is unknown.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents SSTR2+ unresectable/metastatic NETs progressing after ≥1 systemic line. Does not represent SSTR-negative disease or treatment-naive pts.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Efficacy set of 56 pts announced but results not in abstract; cohort 3 efficacy rests on 8 evaluable pts. No PFS, DoR, or central read.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The tolerability signal at 6 mCi is the main deliverable; durable activity is suggested by small numbers only. Whether alpha RLT adds after beta-emitter RLT is not addressed.

studies.interpretation:
The case for an alpha-emitting SSTR2 agent rests on two claims: that the higher linear energy transfer and short path length of alpha particles kill cells that beta emitters leave behind, and that this can be done without paying for it in kidney or marrow. This abstract speaks mainly to the second claim. Across 67 treated pts through the 6 mCi level, the sponsors report no dose-limiting toxicity, no grade 4 or 5 events, no serious renal events and no clinically significant treatment-related myelosuppression. For anyone who has managed cumulative renal and hematologic toxicity after beta-emitter RLT, that is the reassuring part, with the caveat that late renal effects and therapy-related myeloid neoplasms are slow to declare themselves and the follow-up here is measured in months to roughly two years for most pts.

The efficacy claim is much thinner than the safety claim. The 43.4% ORR comes from 23 of 46 cohort 2 pts who had enough follow-up when it was first presented, which is a selection by time on study rather than a full cohort read. The abstract announces a 56-pt efficacy set but does not give its result, and cohort 3 contributes 2 PRs among 8 evaluable pts. Response is investigator-assessed, with no central review stated, and there is no PFS or duration of response. In well-differentiated NETs, where disease can be indolent and SSTR-targeted therapy has historically shown modest objective response with a larger effect on progression, ORR alone is a weak proxy for benefit.

Against 177Lu-DOTATATE, as tested in NETTER-1, the comparison a reader wants is impossible from this source. Eligibility requires progression after at least one systemic line but does not say whether that includes prior beta-emitter RLT. That distinction decides where this agent would sit: as an alternative first RLT, or as a salvage option once beta RLT has failed. A response rate in RLT-naive pts and one in RLT-refractory pts would mean quite different things, and the abstract does not separate them.

What would make the signal wrong? If the responders cluster in the RLT-naive or low-grade subset, if responses prove short, or if the 56-pt set dilutes the early 23-pt figure, the activity claim shrinks to something close to existing RLT with a different isotope. Escalation is also continuing into Cohort 4, so the dose that would carry forward is not settled. The practical read is a credible safety profile through 6 mCi, early activity worth a randomized test, and no basis yet for choosing it over approved RLT outside a trial.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: For the RT reader delivering RLT, the safety read is the kidney and marrow: no serious renal events or clinically significant myelosuppression through 6 mCi in 67 pts. Escalation continues into Cohort 4, so the working dose is not yet fixed.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Population is post-systemic-progression SSTR2+ NETs, the space where sequencing after somatostatin analogues and beta-emitter RLT is open. ORR 43.4% comes from 23 of 46 cohort 2 pts; no PFS, DoR, or prior-RLT breakdown reported in source.

open_questions: Activity after prior 177Lu-DOTATATE versus RLT-naive pts
Durability of response and PFS in full efficacy set
Late renal and marrow toxicity with longer follow-up

sites.intro: Consolidation RT in synchronous OM NSCLC buys local control and PFS, but new distant mets still drive OS.

studies.name: SARON
studies.tldr: Consolidation RT added to 1L SACT: mOS 31.0 vs 28.0 mo, HR 0.99 (p=0.95); mPFS 13.9 vs 8.9 mo, HR 0.64 in synchronous OM AGA-negative NSCLC.
details: 📊 Endpoint OS not met: HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.63–1.55), p=0.95

details.text: 📊 Outcomes by arm, 37.4 mo median f/u

details: 🔍 Randomised (1:1) multicentre phase II, N=140, 22 UK centres, Oct 2016 to Jul 2023
🔍 1–5 synchronous mets in ≤3 organs; randomised after ~6–8 wk SACT with CR/PR/SD

details.text: ☢️ RT delivery: 62/70 (88.6%) of the RT arm received RT
subdetails: Primary ± locoregional nodes in field; dose/fractionation not reported in source

details: 💊 SACT: 40.0% chemo, 15.0% IO, 45.0% chemo-IO; control arm added IO from Jan 2020
⚠️ RT controlled treated sites but did not reduce new distant mets; systemic relapse drove OS
⚠️ Mixed-era systemic backbone; cannot isolate RT effect on a uniform chemo-IO population
⚠️ Phase II size for an OS primary; post-progression salvage RT and subsequent therapy not reported in source
📊 6 pts had G3 events possibly RT-related; EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13 QoL similar between arms
🔗 Gomez phase II (49 pts, pre-IO era) reported mOS 41.2 vs 17.0 mo; SARON does not reproduce the OS signal

verdict.rationale: Randomised, completed analysis with prespecified OS primary clearly null, contradicting the OS rationale from smaller pre-IO trials; PFS/local control gains secondary.
verdict.audience: Synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC, 1–5 mets, 1L SACT non-progressors

studies.significance: The RT effect is confined to treated sites: 12-mo local failure 13.0% vs 39.5%, while new distant metastasis was 36.2% vs 32.3% (p=0.28). Consolidation RT to primary plus SABR to all OM sites buys PFS (HR 0.64) at no added G≥3 toxicity or QoL cost, so the consent conversation shifts from survival to durable site control.
studies.monday_clinic: In synchronous oligometastatic AGA-negative NSCLC responding or stable after 1L SACT, this supports consolidation RT for local control and PFS but questions it as a survival intervention; it does not extend to driver-positive or metachronous oligometastatic disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Randomised (1:1) multicentre phase II**, 140 pts across 22 UK centres, Oct 2016 to Jul 2023. Stratified by SACT, histology, N-stage, number of mets, brain mets and site. Median follow-up 37.4 mo.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Synchronous OM NSCLC without actionable genomic alteration**, 1–5 mets in ≤3 organs, randomised after initial SACT with CR, PR or SD. Median age 68, 58.6% adenocarcinoma, 52.9% N2/3, 62.9% single OM site, 6.4% brain mets.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: SACT was 40.0% chemo, 15.0% IO, 45.0% combination, median 4 cycles in both arms. **Control arm changed to include IO in Jan 2020.**

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Radical RT to the lung primary ± locoregional nodes plus **SABR to all OM sites**. 62/70 (88.6%) received RT: 51 conventional and 11 SABR to primary, 54 SABR to ≥1 OM site. Dose/fractionation not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **OS.** Major secondary: PFS. Also local failure, new distant metastasis, toxicity and EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13 QoL.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **OS not improved; PFS and local control improved; new distant metastasis unchanged.** Arm-level values in the table.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: G≥3 AE rate **28.6% in both arms**; 6 pts had a G3 event possibly related to RT. QoL similar between arms.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The Gomez phase II randomised 49 pts in the pre-IO era and reported mOS 41.2 vs 17.0 mo with local consolidation; SARON, larger and NSCLC-specific, **does not reproduce an OS benefit**. SABR-COMET supported the oligometastatic concept across histologies with few lung pts.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents synchronous OM AGA-negative NSCLC with ≤5 mets in ≤3 organs not progressing on 1L SACT. Does not represent driver-positive, metachronous, or oligoprogressive disease, or a uniformly chemo-IO treated cohort.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Mixed-era systemic backbone with a protocol change mid-accrual. Post-progression therapy, including salvage RT in the control arm, not reported in source, which could dilute an OS difference.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: RT did what it targets, suppressing failure at treated sites, but **new distant metastasis was unchanged**, so occult systemic disease set survival. Consolidation is defensible for site control and PFS, not as a survival claim.

studies.interpretation:
SARON is the largest NSCLC-specific randomised test of consolidating every visible site in synchronous oligometastatic disease, and its central contribution is to split two claims that the field has tended to bundle. The first claim, that comprehensive RT controls the disease it treats, is supported cleanly: cumulative local failure at 12 months fell from 39.5% to 13.0%, and PFS improved with HR 0.64. The second claim, that this control converts into longer life, is not supported: OS HR 0.99 with a confidence interval running from 0.63 to 1.55, and median OS 31.0 versus 28.0 months.

The pattern-of-failure data explain the split better than any speculation about power. New distant metastasis occurred in 36.2% versus 32.3%, no difference. Ablating known lesions did not prevent seeding elsewhere, which is what one would expect if many of these pts carry occult systemic disease that lesion counting cannot detect. That makes SARON less an argument against the oligometastatic concept than an argument that a count of 1 to 5 lesions is a weak selector for the biology that concept assumes.

Against the prior randomised evidence, SARON sits uneasily beside the Gomez phase II, which randomised 49 pts and reported mOS 41.2 versus 17.0 months. That trial was small, pre-IO, and randomised only after systemic response, so its OS signal was always fragile. SARON is larger and enrolled into the IO era, though its backbone was mixed: 40.0% chemotherapy alone, 15.0% IO alone, 45.0% chemo-IO, with IO added to the control arm only from January 2020. The OS question for a uniformly chemo-IO treated population, where durable systemic control is more common and residual disease after response may matter more, is therefore not settled here, and could cut either way.

Two methodological features should temper a reader's confidence in the null OS result without overturning it. A phase II of 140 pts is not designed to exclude a modest OS benefit, and the interval is wide enough to admit one. Post-progression therapy, including salvage RT in control pts who progressed at known sites, is not reported in the source; if common, it would compress any OS difference, which is a real effect of a strategy of deferral rather than a flaw. Neither point rescues an OS claim; both argue against reading HR 0.99 as proof of no effect.

The practical read is that consolidation RT remains reasonable for selected pts who respond to first-line therapy, particularly where a residual lesion threatens morbidity, because the toxicity cost appears small: G≥3 AE 28.6% in both arms, 6 pts with possibly RT-related G3 events, and similar QoL. What changes is the justification. The defensible offer is fewer local failures and longer PFS, not survival. Dose and fractionation were not reported in the source, so whether the local control figures transfer to a given department's schedules remains open. The more consequential next step is selection: response depth, ctDNA, and molecular features are likelier to identify pts in whom ablating residual disease alters the natural history than the number of lesions on a staging scan.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Comprehensive consolidation (radical RT to primary ± nodes, SABR to OM sites) cut 12-mo local failure to 13.0% vs 39.5% with G≥3 AE 28.6% in both arms. The value is site control and PFS, not OS (HR 0.99), which reframes how consolidation is justified to pts and tumour boards.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Adding RT after 1L SACT response did not change OS (31.0 vs 28.0 mo) or new distant metastasis rates, so systemic therapy remains the survival driver. Only 15.0% received IO alone and 45.0% chemo-IO, so the result does not settle consolidation in uniformly chemo-IO treated pts.

open_questions: Does consolidation RT improve OS on a uniform chemo-IO backbone?
Which biomarkers select pts whose OM disease is truly limited?
Role of post-progression salvage RT in diluting OS differences

details: 🔍 Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter; N=703 (349 pembro + dCRT vs 354 pbo + dCRT)

verdict.audience: Untreated unresectable locally advanced ESCC/EAC/GEJ, dCRT candidates

studies.significance: The toxicity signal is the RT-relevant read: grade 5 AEs 13% vs 10% and AE discontinuation 34% vs 27% with pembro, with EFS HR 0.97 and OS HR 1.00 in the enriched CPS ≥10 group. For dCRT at 50 or 60 Gy, concurrent PD-1 blockade adds harm without local or systemic control gain.
studies.monday_clinic: In surgery-ineligible locally advanced esophageal or GEJ cancer with PD-L1 CPS ≥10, this does not support adding concurrent pembrolizumab to dCRT; it does not address adjuvant IO after trimodality therapy and resection.

primary_endpoint.name: Event-free survival (PD-L1 CPS ≥10)
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: 95% CI 0.77-1.23, P=0.3994; did not meet boundary 0.0193

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: International **phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled** multicenter trial, 1:1, **N=703**. Results from the **second interim analysis (IA2)**, median follow-up **47.1 mo** (range 21.7-70.2).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Previously untreated, **unresectable locally advanced** ESCC, EAC or GEJ cancer, **ineligible for curative surgery** but suitable for dCRT, ECOG PS 0-1. Includes cervical or upper thoracic EC with **supraclavicular LN mets only**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Pembro 200 mg or pbo Q3W for 8 cycles, then 400 mg or pbo Q6W for 5 cycles, given with dCRT.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Site-choice dCRT: **FP with RT 50 Gy or 60 Gy**, or **FOLFOX with RT 50 Gy**. Fractionation, target volumes and dose distribution by arm not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Dual primary:** investigator-assessed EFS and OS, tested hierarchically in PD-L1 **CPS ≥10**, then CPS ≥1, then all pts.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: EFS **not improved** in CPS ≥10, so no downstream endpoint was formally tested and **the study was stopped**.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Grade ≥3 AEs in **100%** of both arms. **Grade 5: 13% vs 10%**; AE discontinuation **34% vs 27%**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: dCRT alone, the backbone established since RTOG 85-01, remains the standard for surgery-ineligible disease. The PACIFIC paradigm of IO after chemoRT in NSCLC does not carry over here with concurrent dosing, and this does not address CheckMate 577, which tested adjuvant nivolumab after resection.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents untreated, surgery-ineligible locally advanced ESCC, EAC or GEJ cancer receiving dCRT, with PD-L1 CPS ≥10 for the formally tested endpoint. Does not represent resectable disease on a trimodality pathway or adjuvant IO after surgery.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Histology-specific results and the 50 vs 60 Gy split are not in source, so a benefit confined to one histology or dose cannot be excluded. Locoregional failure patterns are not reported, so the EFS null cannot be broken down into in-field control vs distant spread.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: In the PD-L1-enriched population most likely to benefit, EFS and OS curves did not separate, which argues against a meaningful benefit hidden in lower-CPS groups. The excess grade 5 events need adjudication before any further concurrent IO-dCRT trial goes forward.

studies.interpretation:
The strongest inference from this trial comes from where the null result sits in the testing hierarchy. The investigators put their best chance first: PD-L1 CPS ≥10, the population in which checkpoint blockade has worked most consistently in advanced esophageal cancer. A PD-1 inhibitor added to definitive chemoradiotherapy still produced an EFS hazard ratio of 0.97 and an OS hazard ratio of 1.00 in that group. The lower-CPS and all-comer analyses were never formally tested, but it is hard to build a plausible biological case for a benefit there when the enriched group shows nothing. The practical reading is that dCRT alone remains the backbone for surgery-ineligible locally advanced disease, as it has been since RTOG 85-01.

The design deserves more confidence than most negative IO trials. It was double-blind and placebo-controlled, so EFS assessed by investigators was protected from the bias that usually affects open-label event-driven endpoints, and median follow-up of 47.1 months is long enough that a delayed-separation effect would have had time to show. This was an interim analysis, but the trial was stopped and the observed P-value (0.3994) was far from the boundary (0.0193). Further follow-up is very unlikely to reverse the result.

The safety data matter more than the efficacy data for a radiation oncologist. Grade 5 events in 13% vs 10%, and AE-driven discontinuation in 34% vs 27%, indicate that concurrent PD-1 blockade with esophageal dCRT carries a real cost with no efficacy to offset it. The source does not break these events down by cause, so it is not clear whether the excess comes from pneumonitis, esophagitis, or something unrelated to the overlap of RT and IO. That question decides whether a sequential strategy is worth testing or whether the combination should be dropped entirely.

Several reasons the result could still be misleading for a subset are worth naming. The trial pooled squamous and adenocarcinoma histologies, whose immune biology and response to dCRT differ, and the abstract does not report outcomes by histology. RT dose was left to the site (50 or 60 Gy), so dose heterogeneity is uncontrolled, and patterns of failure are not reported. A histology-restricted signal, or a benefit limited to locoregional control and offset by distant events, cannot be excluded from what is available. None of these would justify off-protocol use. They would justify reading the full histology and failure-pattern data before closing the question.

The contrast with lung cancer is instructive. In NSCLC, the PACIFIC approach gave IO after chemoradiation was complete, not during it. KEYNOTE-975 started pembrolizumab concurrently, and its failure does not by itself rule out consolidation-timed IO in esophageal cancer. It also leaves CheckMate 577, adjuvant nivolumab after trimodality therapy and resection, untouched, because that is a different population at a different decision point.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: dCRT at 50 or 60 Gy remains the standard: concurrent pembro brought grade 5 AEs of 13% vs 10% and discontinuation of 34% vs 27% with no EFS or OS gain in CPS ≥10. Locoregional failure patterns are not reported, so an in-field control effect cannot be judged.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Even PD-L1 CPS ≥10 selection did not identify a benefit: EFS HR 0.97, OS 32.2 vs 35.0 mo. The concurrent pembro schedule (8 cycles Q3W, then 5 cycles Q6W) was given during dCRT, so consolidation-timed IO remains untested by this trial.

open_questions: Does histology (ESCC vs EAC) modify any IO effect with dCRT?
Would IO given after dCRT, not concurrently, change the result?
What drove the excess grade 5 events with pembro?

papers.title: Pembrolizumab or placebo plus concurrent definitive chemoradiotherapy in esophageal and gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) cancer: The phase 3 randomized KEYNOTE-975 study
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2875O · Proffered paper 1: Gastrointestinal tumour, upper digestive · 2026-10-23 · presented by Manish A. Shah (New York, United States of America) · NCT04210115

Background: The role of immunotherapy in participants (pts) with locally advanced, esophageal cancer (EC) treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) is not established. KEYNOTE-975 (NCT04210115) is an international phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo (pbo) controlled multicenter study that examines dCRT ± pembro in pts with previously untreated locally advanced unresectable esophageal and GEJ cancer. We report results from the second interim analysis (IA2).
Methods: Eligible pts with histologically confirmed cTX N+ M0 or cT2-T4a NX M0 esophageal squamous cell cancer (ESCC) or adenocarcinoma (EAC) or GEJ cancer, or cTX N+ M1 cervical or upper thoracic EC with supraclavicular lymph node metastases only, ECOG PS 0-1, and who were ineligible for curative surgery but suitable for dCRT, were randomized 1:1 to 200 mg pembro or pbo Q3W for 8 cycles then 400 mg pembro or pbo Q6W for 5 cycles + site choice of dCRT (5-fluorouracil + cisplatin [FP] with radiotherapy [RT] 50 Gy or 60 Gy, or FOLFOX with RT 50 Gy). Dual-primary endpoints were event-free survival (EFS) by investigator and OS in pts with PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) ≥10, CPS ≥1, and all pts. Data cut-off was Jan 21, 2026.
Results: A total of 703 pts were randomized (349 pembro + dCRT; 354 pbo + dCRT). Median follow-up was 47.1 mo (range, 21.7-70.2) in all pts. At IA2, in pts with PD-L1 CPS ≥10, EFS was not improved with pembro + dCRT vs pbo + dCRT (median 15.2 vs 14.7 mo; HR 0.97; 95% CI, 0.77-1.23 [P=0.3994; P-value boundary for significance 0.0193). In pts with PD-L1 CPS ≥10, median OS was 32.2 mo vs 35.0 mo (HR 1.00; 95% CI, 0.77-1.30 [nominal P-value 0.5003]). As EFS was not positive in PD-L1 CPS ≥10, EFS in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 and all pts, and OS were not tested for statistical significance, and the study was stopped. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 100% of pts in each arm, with grade 5 AEs in 44 (13%) vs 37 (10%) pts. Discontinuation due to any AE occurred in 117 (34%) vs 97 (27%) pts.
Conclusions: Pembrolizumab + dCRT vs pbo + dCRT did not significantly improve EFS in untreated unresectable esophageal or GEJ cancer with PD-L1 CPS ≥10. No new safety signals were observed.
Clinical trial identification: NCT04210115.

papers.title: Primary results of SARON: A randomised-controlled trial of consolidation radiotherapy for synchronous oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2613O · Proffered paper 1: NSCLC, metastatic · 2026-10-25 · presented by Fiona McDonald (London, United Kingdom) · NCT02417662

Background: Standard first-line systemic anti-cancer therapy (SACT) for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable genomic alteration (AGA-negative) is chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy. We investigated whether patients with synchronous oligometastatic (OM) AGA-negative NSCLC benefit from the addition of consolidation radiotherapy (RT).
Methods: SARON, a multicentre phase II trial, randomised (1:1) patients with NSCLC, 1–5 metastases in ≤3 organs, to SACT with or without radical RT. The control arm changed to include immunotherapy in January 2020. The experimental arm received radical RT to the lung primary ± locoregional lymph nodes, and stereotactic ablative RT (SABR) to OM sites. Stratification included SACT, histology, N-stage, number of metastases, brain metastases and recruiting site. Primary and major secondary endpoints were overall (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS).
Results: 140 patients were randomised across 22 UK centres (October 2016 to July 2023). Median age was 68 years (range 45–85), 59.3% male, 58.6% adenocarcinoma, 52.9% N-stage 2/3, 62.9% 1x OM site (23.6% 2x, 9.3% 3x, 3.6% 4x, 0.7% 5x OM sites), and 6.4% brain metastases. SACT was 40.0% chemotherapy, 15.0% immunotherapy and 45.0% combination. Median SACT cycles received in both arms was 4, and 62/70 (88.6%) received RT (51 conventional and 11 SABR to primary, 54 SABR to ≥1 OM site). After 37.4 months median follow-up, median OS was 31.0 versus 28.0 months (HR=0.99, 95%CI 0.63–1.55, p=0.95) and median PFS 13.9 versus 8.9 months (HR=0.64, 95%CI 0.43–0.95, p=0.03) in the SACT+RT and SACT arms, respectively. The cumulative incidence of local failure within 12 months was 13.0% versus 39.5% (p<0.01), compared to 36.2% versus 32.3% (p=0.28) for new distant metastasis, respectively. The grade ≥3 adverse event rate was 28.6% in both arms; 6 patients had a grade 3 event possibly related to RT. EORTC QLQ-C30 and LC13 quality of life measures were similar in both arms.
Conclusions: Patients with synchronous OM AGA-negative NSCLC receiving first-line SACT+RT achieved better local disease control and longer PFS than SACT alone with acceptable side-effects, however, this did not translate into survival benefit.
Clinical trial identification: NCT02417662.

papers.title: Towards organ preservation and cure via immunotherapy in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma patients, normally undergoing extensive curative surgery and radiotherapy (MATISSE 2)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2486RO · Rapid oral: Melanoma and other skin tumours · 2026-10-25 · presented by Stan W. Van Dijk (Amsterdam, Netherlands) · NCT06823479

Background: The MATISSE trial (NCT04620200) showed that 80% of patients with a cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) and an indication for extensive curative surgery with or without adjuvant radiotherapy as standard of care (SOC) reached a partial or major pathological response following two courses of neoadjuvant nivolumab and ipilimumab (NIVO/IPI). In addition, 9 patients reached a clinical complete remission (CCR) after only two courses of NIVO/IPI, without SOC. This raised the question whether organ preservation and cure can be reached via only ultra-short neoadjuvant NIVO/IPI, without SOC and without maintenance immunotherapy.
Methods: In the MATISSE 2 trial (NCT06823479), 41 CSCC patients with an indication for extensive or disfiguring curative surgery will be treated with neoadjuvant NIVO (weeks 0 & 2) and IPI (only week 0). Response evaluation is performed in week 5. In case of a non-response, patients undergo SOC in week 6. In case of a clinical response following NIVO/IPI, we will withhold SOC and patients enter a strict wait-and-monitoring programme.
Results: So far, thirty-one patients have been included (median follow-up of 8 months). Overall, 22/31 (71%) patients showed a clinical response in week 5 and did not undergo SOC per protocol, of whom 15/31 (48%) achieved a CCR and 7/31 (23%) achieved a partial clinical response (PCR) during their wait-and-monitoring program. In total 9/31 (29%) patients received SOC, of whom one patient showed a complete pathological response in the surgical specimen. Immune-related toxicity (19% grade 3-4) was well manageable. There was no delay in surgery due to immune-related toxicity.
Conclusions: Overall, 71% of patients reached a clinical response and did not undergo surgery. So far, 48% of patients reached a CCR following only ultra-short neoadjuvant NIVO/IPI, without SOC and without maintenance immunotherapy. Longer follow-up is required to investigate further deepening of the response in PCR patients and the durability of the response in CCR patients.
Clinical trial identification: NCT06823479 EU trial nr 2024-516152-17-00.

papers.title: Cohort level safety and efficacy results for [212Pb]VMT-a-NET in advanced somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2+)-expressing neuroendocrine tumors (NETs): Cohorts 1–3
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 2396RO · Rapid oral: NETs and endocrine tumours · 2026-10-23 · presented by Thorvardur R. Halfdanarson (Rochester, United States of America) · NCT05636618

Background: [212Pb]VMT-a-NET is an alpha-particle radiopharmaceutical targeting somatostatin receptor type 2 (SSTR2)-expressing tumors. We present safety and efficacy results from the dose-escalation phase 1/2a clinical trial (NCT05636618).
Methods: Eligible participants (pt) for this study must have unresectable or metastatic NETs, documented radiologic progression following at least 1 prior systemic treatment, and evidence of SSTR2 expression in ≥1 lesion confirmed on an FDA approved SSTR PET scan. During the dose finding phase, pts may receive up to 4 administrations of [212Pb]VMT-a-NET at their assigned dose level, and they are monitored for dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) for 42 days and safety throughout the study. Efficacy is evaluated by investigators according to RECIST criteria v1.1.
Results: As of 03Apr2026, 67 pts have been enrolled in the study and received at least 1 dose of [212Pb]VMT-α-NET: 2 pts in dose Cohort 1 (2.5 mCi), 46 in Cohort 2 (5 mCi), and 19 in Cohort 3 (6 mCi). No DLTs, Grade 4 or 5 adverse events, treatment-related discontinuations, serious renal events, dysphagia, or clinically significant treatment-related myelosuppression have been observed. Efficacy evaluation was previously performed and presented for cohort 1 and a subset of pts of cohort 2 (n=23/46) who had sufficient duration of follow up (96.4 wks and 60.1 wks, respectively) and an ORR in cohort 2 of 43.4%. The presented efficacy set will include 56 pts (n=2 in Cohorts 1, n=46 in 2, and n= 8 in Cohort 3). Among the DLT Cohort 3, 2 pts achieved a PR after 1 and 2 cycles. Both pts in Cohort 1 continued to exhibit stable disease after 2 years of follow up.
Conclusions: Treatment with [212Pb]VMT-α-NET demonstrates a favorable safety profile across all treated pts (n=67) and shows signs of sustained efficacy at the 2.5, 5, and 6 mCi dose levels. The therapy is well tolerated with no observed dose-limiting toxicities or serious treatment-related adverse events. This study is ongoing and enrolling into Cohort 4.
Clinical trial identification: NCT05636618.
